I have written HTML in 39 public repositories, from 2014 to 2026; in 5 of them it is the main language.

What it was for: [Tools](@/projects/tools.md) (10), [Data and GIS](@/projects/data.md) (8), [Web](@/projects/web.md) (8) and [Media and art](@/projects/media.md) (5).

Most recently: [Oscilla](@/work/oscilla.md): Generate, measure and reproduce sound experiments, and know how far each result can be trusted. Every readout carries its uncertainty; [prismatic-flipperzero](@/work/prismatic-flipperzero.md): Prismatic for Flipper Zero: native FAP on its way to Prismatic Pocket, an offline evidence-first epistemic toolkit; [Majordomus](@/work/prismatic-majordomus.md): One policy for every AI coding tool, scoped tasks with a finish contract, a mesh for many sessions and machines, and an integration queue that lands only verified work. Local; it never invokes a model.

17 of these projects run as live sites.

I also used it in client work under confidentiality agreements. Roles: Architect, Lead engineer, AI engineer, Data engineer, Investigator and Advisor. What was solved: LLM agents, Decision support, AI transformation, Audit trail and OSINT investigation. The use cases below give the principle and the intent of that work; no client, person, date or number is named.

How to read the evidence: every [repository](@/glossary/repository.md) below is measured from GitHub and GitLab (every 6 hours) and says how it uses HTML: as the main language, as a measured share of its code, in its declared stack or as a topic. The reference graph links HTML to the repositories and to the other languages and technologies they use together.
